contracts.boundary: Regex route rules from any configuration source cannot stall the host event loop at pipeline construction or per message. compileRules rejects superlinear patterns structurally from the pattern text (an unbounded-quantified group whose body carries a variable quantifier, or an alternation whose branches split subjects ambiguously through prefix-overlap or an empty branch) and keeps canary probes under a per-canary wall-clock budget with a required re-measure override as the backstop for unnamed families; the deprecated classify() path applies the same guard so both paths drop the identical set and preserve rule-order precedence. The strategy selection is total at the injectable random seam: every value the seam returns, including values outside [0,1) and NaN, selects a candidate instead of returning undefined.
contracts.assertions: Catastrophic families (nested quantifier, repeated group, branch-overlap alternation) and their lookahead-anchored dodge variants are dropped at compile without executing the regular expression, so rejection cannot pay a long probe; benign quantified rules (fixed-length tokens, bounded ambiguity-free alternations) and every shipped default rule still compile. The legacy classify() path drops the same catastrophic pattern the compiled path drops (parity for the audit's hang case), and rule-order precedence across match positions is preserved in both paths. A simulated scheduler pause inside one elapsed-time sample does not reject a benign rule, because a canary must over-run the budget twice, once on re-measure, before rejection. Random selection with seam values -1, NaN, 1, and 0.999999 picks a defined candidate, and in-range values keep candidate-index parity.

boundaryTest.name: drops rule patterns whose backtracking explodes on a small canary

invariant.name: still compiles every shipped default rule

fault.name: keeps the injectable random seam total when it returns 1

contracts.boundary: The TypeSafe classifier bounds how much provider response body it materializes while decoding the streamed judgment JSON, so a hostile or stuck endpoint degrades to a classifier miss instead of growing process memory without limit.
contracts.assertions: A response whose accumulated body exceeds the 1 MiB decode budget is treated as an invalid response: the classification returns undefined, the observation reports invalid_response, and the stream is cancelled. A response within the budget decodes normally, and deadline/abort behavior of the reader is unchanged.

boundaryTest.name: treats an oversized response body as an invalid response

invariant.name: aborts and cancels a stalled response body at deadline

fault.exception: The faulty implementation (an unbounded reader) was the shipped code this change replaced; the named boundary test failed against it before the fix was written and passes after, which is the recorded controlled-fault proof. Injecting the unbounded reader again would only re-run that same recorded red.

The set-based membership check duplicated the literal not-automatic condition already enforced.
contracts.assertions: Explicit, pinned, disabled, and non-user targets still report not_applicable without echoing caller labels; unknown labels fail closed to not_applicable; automatic targets keep the full advisory evidence path. No export or type changes.

boundaryTest.name: does not advise on explicit, pinned, disabled, or non-user targets

invariant.name: fails closed on unknown origins without echoing caller labels

There is no faulty implementation exercising the removed branch to inject, and the collapse behavior itself is covered by the named boundary and invariant tests.
